case_name: Mohd. Rashid Ahmad and another v State Of U.P. & Anr
facts: The case involves appeals by special leave against the judgment of the Allahabad High Court dated May 12, 1969.
Mohd. Rashid Ahmad was a permanent Assistant Engineer in the Development Board, Kanpur, and Ashfaq Hussain was a permanent Sanitary Inspector in the Municipal Board, Kanpur.
The State Government constituted Municipal Corporations in five cities in the State, namely Kanpur, Agra, Varanasi, Allahabad and Lucknow w.e.f. February 1, 1960.
An Administrator was appointed of both the Development Board and the Municipal Board, Kanpur, under the U.P. Local Bodies (Appointment of Administrators) Act, 1953.
The appellant Mohd. Rashid Ahmad was appointed as Offg. Executive Engineer by the Administrator of the Municipal Corporation, Kanpur, for a period of one year on September 12, 1960.
Ashfaq Hussain was transferred in the same capacity to the Municipal Corporation, Allahabad, where he was promoted temporarily as an Assistant Engineer.
issues: Whether the State Government's rules providing for the creation of Centralised Palika Services were valid and effective
Whether the State Government had the power to make retrospective rules
Whether the procedure followed by the State Government in finalising action on absorption of officers and servants was valid
petitioner_arguments: The petitioners argued that the State Government's rules providing for the creation of Centralised Palika Services were invalid and ineffective
They contended that the State Government did not have the power to make retrospective rules
They claimed that the procedure followed by the State Government in finalising action on absorption of officers and servants was invalid
respondent_arguments: The respondents argued that the State Government's rules providing for the creation of Centralised Palika Services were valid and effective
They contended that the State Government had the power to make retrospective rules
They defended the procedure followed by the State Government in finalising action on absorption of officers and servants
court_reasoning: The Court held that the State Government's rules providing for the creation of Centralised Palika Services were valid and effective
It ruled that the State Government had the power to make retrospective rules
It found that the procedure followed by the State Government in finalising action on absorption of officers and servants was valid
holding: The Court dismissed the appeals and upheld the judgment of the Allahabad High Court dated May 12, 1969.
